newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-TOULOUSE HUMBLED BY DAZZLING WASPS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-TOULOUSE HUMBLED BY DAZZLING WASPS.

text.p: Defending champions Toulouse slumped to the heaviest defeat suffered by a French club side in the short history of rugby union's European Cup on Saturday.

The Frenchmen were hammered 77-17 by English opponents Wasps, previously without a win in the tournament, and must now win their final match against Munster next weekend to qualify for the quarter-finals.

They conceded nine tries as Wasps produced some dazzling rugby, leaking 54 points after half-time as full-back Jon Ufton landed 11 kicks from 12 attempts for the home side. Toulouse also lost international Thomas Castaignede through injury.
The only way Wasps can now qualify is if Milan upset Cardiff on Sunday, but it was still a notable day for England's top clubs at the expense of French opposition.
Bath beat Dax 25-16 with 17 points from captain Jonathan Callard, despite a superb performance in the line-out from captain Olivier Roumat.

Jonathan Callard kicked 17 points for Bath and converted a crucial try from rugby league recruit Henry Paul, although Dax still have a superior goal difference going into the final round of pool matches next weekend.
Leicester became the only English side definitely through to the last eight after edging out Pau 19-14 in a close-fought encounter in France.

The difference between the sides proved to be a superb second-half try from 19-year-old winger Leon Lloyd, justifying Leicester coach Bob Dwyer's decision to select him ahead of England's record try-scorer Rory Underwood.
Leicester trailed 14-6 at half-time, but Lloyd's 50-metre run in the 51st minute added to 14 points from kicker Rob Liley secured the English side's third straight win.
Pau must now win their final match against Leinster in Dublin next weekend to have any hope of qualifying for the knock-out stages.
There will be more keen Anglo-French rivalry on Sunday when Brive host Harlequins in a game likely to determine the winners of Pool C.
